questions.prompt: Which expansion of "The technician repairs the radio" keeps active voice and adds a first conditional in the simple present form?
choices: If the technician repaired the radio quickly, the customer would be happy.
If the technician repairs the radio quickly, the customer will be happy.
If the technician repairs the radio quickly, the customer is happy.
The radio is repaired quickly by the technician.
questions.explanation: The correct option uses a present-tense if-clause and will in the result while keeping the technician as the active subject.
questions.skill: Expanding with an active first conditional
questions.topic: Expand a Sentence - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which expansion of The principal expects the athletes to arrive early keeps active voice and uses the subjunctive mood?

The principal expects that each athlete is arriving early.
questions.explanation: The active verb expects introduces a that-clause in which arrive takes the subjunctive form rather than the indicative forms arrives, will arrive, or is arriving.

kept.prompt: Which expansion of The pharmacist checks the prescription shifts the main action to passive voice and uses a first conditional in the simple present form?
choices: If the pharmacist checks the prescription, it will be sent to the pharmacy.
If the pharmacist checked the prescription, it would be sent to the pharmacy.
If the pharmacist had checked the prescription, it would have been sent to the pharmacy.
If the pharmacist is checking the prescription, it will be sent to the pharmacy.
kept.explanation: The if-clause uses the simple present and the will-clause states the likely result, while it will be sent is passive.
kept.skill: Combining passive voice with a first conditional

kept.prompt: Which expansion of The curator archives the photographs changes to passive voice and uses the subjunctive mood?
choices: It is essential that the photographs be archived by the curator.
It is essential that the curator archive the photographs.
The photographs are archived by the curator every winter.
The curator archives the photographs when the exhibition ends.
kept.explanation: This sentence uses the passive voice with a subjunctive base form, be archived, to express necessity.

kept.prompt: Which expansion of The coach posts the schedule keeps active voice and adds a first conditional in the simple present form?
choices: If the coach posts the schedule early, the players will receive it sooner.
If the coach posted the schedule early, the players would receive it sooner.
The schedule will be posted by the coach early so the players will receive it sooner.
If the schedule is posted early, the players will receive it sooner.
kept.explanation: This sentence uses the present-tense if-clause and will-future main clause of a first conditional while keeping the coach as the active subject.
kept.skill: Expanding a sentence with active voice and a first conditional

rejected.prompt: Which of the following expands the sentence "The manager reviewed the report" by shifting to passive voice and adding a conditional mood?
choices: The report was reviewed by the manager, and he would approve it.
The report would be reviewed by the manager if he had time.
The manager reviews the report, and he will approve it.
The report is reviewed by the manager, and he approves it.
rejected.explanation: The correct expansion uses the passive construction "would be reviewed" and a conditional "if he had time" to shift both voice and mood.
rejected.reason: B: not exactly one correct (Option (0) also has passive voice and adds a clause with the conditional auxiliary “would,” so both (0) and (1) are defensible.)

rejected.prompt: Which version expands "They will announce the results" by changing to passive voice and adding an indicative future mood?
choices: The results will be announced by them.
The results would be announced by them if they could.
The results are announced by them tomorrow.
The results were announced by them yesterday.
rejected.explanation: The correct expansion keeps the future indicative "will be announced" while converting the active verb to passive voice.
rejected.reason: B: not exactly one correct (Option (2) is also passive and indicative with future time expressed by “tomorrow,” so the wording does not uniquely select (0).)

rejected.prompt: Which of the following expands "We must submit the application" by shifting to passive voice and subjunctive mood?
choices: The application must be submitted by us.
The application would be submitted by us if we were required.
We submit the application, and it is accepted.
The application is submitted by us, and it gets accepted.
rejected.explanation: The correct expansion employs the passive subjunctive "would be submitted" together with a conditional "if we were required" to achieve the required shifts.
rejected.reason: A: picked -1 not 1 (No option correctly combines passive voice with subjunctive mood)

rejected.prompt: Which expansion of The courier delivers the parcel shifts to passive voice and uses the past perfect indicative mood?
choices: The courier had delivered the parcel before noon.
The parcel was delivered by the courier at noon.
The parcel had been delivered by the courier before noon.
The parcel was being delivered by the courier at noon.
rejected.explanation: The passive construction had been delivered places the parcel as the receiver of the action, and had been marks the past perfect indicative form.
rejected.reason: source: "Past perfect is formed with 'had' + past participle.": not_addressed

rejected.prompt: Which expansion of The council repairs the damaged road shifts to passive voice and uses a second conditional mood?
choices: If the council repaired the damaged road more often, traffic delays would be reduced.
If the council repairs the damaged road more often, traffic delays will be reduced.
If the council had repaired the damaged road more often, traffic delays would have been reduced.
The damaged road is repaired more often by the council, so traffic delays would be reduced.
rejected.explanation: The past-tense if-clause and would-clause form a second conditional, while the main clause uses passive voice.

rejected.prompt: Which expansion of The teacher suggests a hands-on science project keeps active voice and uses a subjunctive that-clause?
choices: The teacher suggests that a hands-on science project be built by the class.
The teacher suggests that the class build a hands-on science project.
The teacher suggests that the class is building a hands-on science project.
The teacher suggests that the class should build a hands-on science project.
rejected.explanation: The bare verb build expresses the subjunctive mood, and the class remains the subject of the active that-clause.

rejected.prompt: Which expansion of The baker kneads the dough changes to passive voice and uses a third conditional indicative mood?
choices: If the baker had kneaded the dough, the bread would have risen better.
If the baker kneads the dough, the bread will rise better.
If the baker kneaded the dough, the bread would rise better.
If the dough was kneaded by the baker, the bread would have risen better.
rejected.explanation: This sentence uses the third conditional by pairing the past perfect had kneaded with the future perfect would have risen while placing the action in the passive voice.
